title: Chicago Marks Diwali With Fireworks, Temple Programmes and Feasts
excerpt: Bartlett's BAPS mandir lit the sky on Saturday, Chopda Pujan followed on Diwali Sunday, and celebrations continue in the Chicago area on November 10.
body:
• Diwali fell on Sunday, November 8, 2026, and the Chicago area marked it across the weekend — headlined by the BAPS mandir's fireworks and sound show in Bartlett on Saturday night.
  • At BAPS Chicago, food stalls ran from 5:00 to 7:45 p.m. and fireworks followed at 8:00 p.m., with offsite parking at Bartlett High School and shuttles through 9:00 p.m.
  • Sunday's observances at the mandir included Chopda Pujan, the blessing of account books for a fresh start.
  • The programme is not over: BAPS Chicago lists further Diwali events on Tuesday, November 10, 2026 — see the mandir's events page for timings before you go.

Chicago's Diwali weekend ran from temple courtyards to banquet halls. With the festival itself falling on Sunday, November 8, 2026, communities across the city and suburbs spread their celebrations across the days around it — fireworks in Bartlett on Saturday, account-book blessings on Sunday, and association dinners that began weeks earlier.

Fireworks in Bartlett

The weekend's largest public gathering was at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Bartlett, northwest of Chicago. Its Diwali Fireworks and Sound Show on Saturday, November 7, paired food stalls, open from 5:00 to 7:45 p.m., with an 8:00 p.m. fireworks display the mandir describes as a fusion of light, music and cultural programming. Entrance to the mandir stopped at 7:45 p.m., and visitors arriving after 5:00 p.m. were directed to offsite parking at Bartlett High School, 701 W. Schick Road, with shuttle service to the mandir from 5:00 to 9:00 p.m. The mandir is at 1851 S. IL Route 59 (Pramukh Swami Road), Bartlett, IL 60103.

Sunday's observances at BAPS included Chopda Pujan, the blessing of account books to mark a fresh beginning, according to BizzBuzz's roundup of Diwali across the US and Canada, which also noted festive menus running at Chicago restaurants through Sunday. BAPS Chicago's own programme continues on Tuesday, November 10, with its remaining Diwali events — the mandir's events page carries the current schedule.

A 35th anniversary in Downers Grove

The celebrations began earlier for one of the area's longest-running community groups. The UP Association of Greater Chicago marked Diwali and its 35th anniversary on Sunday, October 25, 2026, at Ashyana Banquet Hall, 1620 75th Street in Downers Grove, according to Hi India. Founded in October 1991, the association brought families together for music, dance, Hindi poetry and dinner, opening with the ceremonial lighting of the diya and a Ganesh Vandana dance. Dr. M. Anand Prakash, Consul General of India in Chicago, attended as chief guest.

Association president Uma Agarwal described the evening as a family reunion, and co-founder Dr. Subhash Pandey pointed to the group's annual Kavi Sammelan and its Diwali and Holi gatherings as the thread keeping families connected to Hindi language and literature across generations — including performances by young people growing up in the United States.

What the weekend shows

Taken together, the Chicago calendar followed the pattern visible across North America this year: the festival anchored at temples and community halls, carried into restaurants and public spaces, and stretched across the weekends on either side of the day itself so families could attend more than one celebration. For Chicago-area readers still looking to mark the festival, the BAPS programme on November 10 is the next listed date.
